argument:
The bull correctly identifies CFO of RM2.391bn versus RM1.060bn as a cash measure distinct from fair-value and remeasurement additions to profit. That answers a claim that all improvement is noncash. It does not establish recurring distributable cash: acquisition outlays, maintenance investment and funding demands still need a matched bridge, while borrowings rose to RM25.353bn from RM19.590bn.

RM855.177m property fair-value gains and RM502.789m JV remeasurement qualify the headline P/E of 8.54x; Q4 owners profit also fell to RM523.111m from RM823.930m. The enlarged asset base may eventually earn adequate returns, but these returns have not been demonstrated after its obligations. A downtrend and oversold RSI offer no proof of a bottom. I favor cash-return verification before treating low reported earnings valuation as actionable.
key_points: CFO growth proves some cash improvement, not post-investment surplus.
Borrowings increased and acquisition funding needs reconciliation.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's CFO counterargument is valid and narrows the accounting objection. It still leaves the debt-funded asset-return and recurring-earnings questions unanswered, so it cannot establish that 8.54x reported earnings represents buying value.
